task.description: This is a DESIGN-FIRST issue (ISS-0430) -- no fix, no implementation. Your job at Step 0.5/1 is narrower than a normal diagnosis: the issue filing's own evidence is already first-hand (a grep run 2026-09-03, re-verified by ORCH 2026-09-05 with zero hits for Postgrex.Notifications/LISTEN/NOTIFY/Phoenix.PubSub across lib/, and specific dev-host profiling numbers already in the issue text) and ORCH has already corrected the filing's stale premise (REQ-214 and ISS-0425's own follow-on requirements REQ-219/REQ-220 have all shipped as 'done', changing the sequencing question from greenfield to retrofit -- see ISS-0430.yaml's own 'SEQUENCING NOTE' paragraph for the full correction). Read that file in full before starting; it is the task, not merely background. Do these three things: (1) Step 0.5 registry lookup -- grep docs/issues/*.yaml for any PRIOR resolved/instrumented/no_defect entry whose description mentions NOTIFY, LISTEN, PubSub, or polling-vs-push tradeoffs, and state in your result whether a match exists (expected: none, since the grep in the issue text found zero usage anywhere in lib/, but check the ISSUE REGISTRY specifically -- a design discussion could have happened without any code existing yet). (2) Pull the EXACT current poll-interval/config-key mechanics for both already-shipped pollers CODE-DESIGNER will need to reconcile the design against: read lib/letflow/scheduler.ex (or wherever Letflow.Scheduler.Poller's poll_interval_ms/0-equivalent lives) and lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex's Poller submodule, and report each one's current poll interval (the actual configured/default value, quoting the code), its config key name, and its claim query shape (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, per-tenant schema iteration) in enough detail that CODE-DESIGNER does not need to re-read those files from scratch. (3) Confirm INV-1's exact schema-per-tenant mechanism one more time by reading docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's Dimension B section (already cited in security-invariants.md) and quote its own text on how a query is scoped by :prefix -- this is the mechanism the design's tenant-isolation answer (design question 2) has to reconcile a database-global NOTIFY channel against, so CODE-DESIGNER needs the precise mechanism in hand, not a paraphrase. Do NOT design the fix yourself and do NOT write to lib/letflow/design/ -- that is CODE-DESIGNER's job at the next step. Complete this handoff with your findings in result.summary and route to CODE-DESIGNER.
